one_liner: Firecrawl provides a public HTTP API, free self-serve credentials, and an official MCP server, with different capabilities across cloud and self-hosted deployments.

auth.notes: OAuth is documented for apps connecting users’ accounts; API keys support a team’s own calls. A few REST endpoints require no credential.

access.notes: The self-serve free path uses a Firecrawl Cloud API key. Self-hosting is another path, but requires operating the stack and additional configuration for some capabilities.

api.notes: The public reference covers web-data operations including crawling and monitoring.

mcp.notes: Firecrawl documents a hosted MCP server and publishes server code.

verdict.rationale: Developers can sign up for a free API key, and the public REST reference documents web-data operations including crawling and monitoring. OAuth is documented for apps that connect users’ Firecrawl accounts.

evidence.quote: Your app gets an fco_ access token that works on the REST API in place of an API key, plus an fcr_ refresh token.
API key Create a key in the dashboard and send it on every request as Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR-API-KEY .
A few REST endpoints also work with no credential at all, so you can try Firecrawl before you have a key.
Sign up for a free API key to use every endpoint with higher limits.
Both paths expose Firecrawl’s core APIs; the difference is who configures, secures, and runs the supporting services.
Core scraping works in the default stack; LLM-backed formats, advanced scraping services, and specialized extraction paths need additional configuration.
The Firecrawl API gives you programmatic access to web data. All endpoints share a common base URL, authentication scheme, and response format described on this page.
Monitor Schedule recurring checks and get notified when content changes. Crawl Crawl entire websites and get content from all pages.
Set up Firecrawl MCP with keyless access, account sign-in, or an API key.

A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that brings Firecrawl , the context API for AI agents, to MCP-compatible clients: search, scrape, and interact with the live web and get back clean Markdown or structured data.
Firecrawl automates web crawling and data extraction, enabling organizations to gather content, index sites, and gain insights from online sources at scale
Sign up for a free API key to use every endpoint with higher limits.
To let users connect their own Firecrawl account to your app instead, use OAuth for apps .

verification.note: Quotes show an app access token plus refresh token used in place of an API key (oauth2), a dashboard API key sent as Authorization: Bearer (fairly api_key), and some REST endpoints with no credential. Nothing recommends a different method for third-party apps.

"Sign up for a free API key" proves self_serve_free with no payment, trial, or approval. The open-source-or-cloud quotes support both deployments and that self-hosting needs extra configuration for some capabilities.
The public reference describes endpoints, a shared base URL, auth, and response format, and auth quotes call it a REST API. Crawl and monitor examples do not contradict breadth broad.
Vendor docs say to set up Firecrawl MCP and the firecrawl GitHub repo publishes the server. Setup language shows it is usable now; nothing labels it beta, pilot, or unlaunched.
The quote is on a Composio toolkit page for Firecrawl, so in_catalog yes is shown.
self_serve_free credentials plus a documented public REST API of useful breadth yield buildable_now with main_blocker none.
